correctness.rationale: The proof derives a bijection from each strict-compatible extension to a lower ideal and upper filter, then partitions all nonempty lower ideals by their coordinate maxima (i,j). Each maxima stratum has J(i-1,j-1) ideals; exactly one contains (i,j), creating precisely one invalid upper filter. A marked monotone lattice path bijection evaluates the double convolution after inclusion-exclusion at two terminal boundaries. Algebraic types are restored exactly once per named parameter. Stirling and leading coefficient calculations are explicit. Independent exhaustive ternary transitivity checks cover 24 small grids and corroborate the general identity; they are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The family of finite rectangular products of chains is a canonical two-parameter family of finite distributive lattices and a natural test of finite-stabilizer orbit complexity in a homogeneous structure. The exact all-size one-type spectrum is not the textbook one-chain answer nor an arbitrary small instance. The corner correction and interior-vertex marked lattice paths expose the mechanism, yielding a uniform bivariate formula and a demonstrable polynomial fixed-width versus exponential-square growth dichotomy. These quantitatively describe a meaningful tractable subclass of a generally #P-complete enumeration, without asserting efficient counting for all posets.
